articles.title: GTA 6 launch day guide: release date, platforms, pre-load and download size
articles.dek: GTA VI is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Here's what reviewers made of it, how big the download is, and what to sort out before you start.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI launched on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after two delays that pushed it back from fall 2025 and then from May 2026. It's coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only. There is no PS4 or Xbox One version, and Rockstar hasn't announced a PC release.
## What the reviews say
Critics were close to unanimous. The PS5 version holds a Metacritic score of 99 from more than 150 reviews, matching the all-time record, and OpenCritic also has it at 99. IGN, GameSpot, Game Informer and Eurogamer all gave full marks.
The recurring complaints are small but worth knowing: the game is locked to 30 frames per second on both consoles, some reviewers saw frame drops in busy areas and big police shootouts, and several found the story slows down in later chapters.
Rockstar has said there are no microtransactions in either edition at launch.
## Pre-loading
If you bought the game digitally, pre-loading opened on November 10. If you're only starting the download now, expect to wait a while. Boxed copies work differently: the box holds a download code rather than a disc, and those codes became available from November 12.
## Clear some space
The download is large, up to 212 GB depending on your console. That's a big chunk of a standard PS5 or Series X drive, so check your free space before you start. An approved expansion drive is worth considering if you're short.
## The pre-order bonus
Anyone who buys before November 20 gets the Vintage Vice City Pack, which includes a classic '55 Vapid Stanier sedan, a garage, outfits for both leads and a weapon pattern. Digital buyers also get a free month of GTA+. See our editions guide for the full breakdown.
Work through the checklist below before you start. It remembers what you've ticked in this browser.
checklist: Confirm your copy is bought (digital or boxed code)
Redeem your boxed download code, if you have one
Free up around 212 GB of storage
Install the latest console system update

articles.title: GTA 6 Standard vs Ultimate Edition: what the extra $20 gets you
articles.dek: The Standard Edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. Both play the same story. Here's what the upgrade adds and who it's worth it for.
articles.body:
Rockstar is selling two versions of GTA VI. Both contain the full game and the same story. The difference is a bundle of extra single-player items that come with the Ultimate Edition.
## What every pre-order gets
The Vintage Vice City Pack comes with any copy bought before November 20, Standard or Ultimate:
- A '55 Vapid Stanier sedan and a Shore Court garage with a weapon locker and a drop-off point for fencing goods
- Retro outfits and hairstyles for Jason and Lucia
- A tropical palm-tree pattern for most weapons
- One free month of GTA+ on digital pre-orders
## What the Ultimate Edition adds
- Extra vehicles, including a '95 Grotti Cheetah, a '67 Vapid Dominator buggy with its own garage, a Shitzu Squalo boat, a Dinka Enduro bike and a kayak
- Extra revolvers and personalized versions of two pistols
- Vice City-style outfits and tattoos
- Two extra pieces of content: a raid on a PTT Youngin$ compound and a classic-car job for a character named Wyman
- Access to five shops: Rideout Customs, Sara's Unisex Salon, Stock 305, Electric Fang Tattoo and One-Eyed Willie's
## Our verdict
For most players, the Standard Edition is enough. The Ultimate items give you a head start on cars, guns and style, but none of it changes the story. The Ultimate Edition is digital only, so if you want a box on the shelf, Standard is your only choice. And there's no rush: Standard owners can buy the Ultimate upgrade later if they decide they want it.

articles.title: Jason Duval
articles.dek: One of GTA VI's two playable leads: an Army veteran from a family of hustlers, doing jobs for drug runners in the Keys and looking for a way out.
articles.body:
Jason is one of the two characters you play in GTA VI. Rockstar's profile describes a man who grew up surrounded by grifters and small-time crooks, joined the Army to get away from a rough youth, and came home to find the same life waiting for him. These days he does work for drug runners in the Keys.
## What we know
- He lives in a property owned by Brian Heder, an old-school smuggler, and helps Brian out in return.
- His friend Cal Hampton is part of the same circle around Brian.
- His relationship with Lucia Caminos is at the heart of the story. The trailers frame them as a criminal couple, and many fans compare them to Bonnie and Clyde.
- The trailers suggest the pair end up working with veteran bank robber Raul Bautista.
## His missions
Jason's story starts with Gone Fishing, the second mission, where he and Cal collect a drop for a pilot named Donnie. See the Crime Beat for our walkthrough.
## Still to come
We'll add more of his story missions, safehouses and key moments to this page after launch, with spoilers hidden behind a tap.

articles.title: Lucia Caminos
articles.dek: GTA VI's other lead: a fighter fresh out of Leonida Penitentiary, chasing the better life her mother wanted for the family.
articles.body:
Lucia is GTA VI's second playable character, and the first woman to lead a GTA game in the modern era. Her father taught her to fight from a young age. According to Rockstar's profile, that toughness landed her in Leonida Penitentiary after she fought for her family, and she got out partly through luck.
## What we know
- Her family's story stretches back to Liberty City, the series' take on New York. Her mother has wanted a better life for them ever since.
- She and Jason are a couple, and the game is built around the two of them deciding how far to go together.
- The trailers show her alongside Jason in heists and robberies, apparently including jobs set up by Raul Bautista.
## Her missions
Her story starts in the Prologue, the game's first mission; see the Crime Beat for our walkthrough.
## Still to come
We'll add more of her story missions, key choices and side content after launch. Major plot points will be hidden behind a spoiler tap, so you can read this page safely at any point in the game.

articles.title: Cal Hampton
articles.dek: Jason's homebody friend, who'd rather sit at home with a beer, eavesdrop on the Coast Guard and read up on conspiracy theories.
facts: Listening in on Coast Guard radio
articles.body:
Cal is Jason's friend and another member of Brian Heder's circle in the Keys. Where Jason wants something bigger, Cal is happy where he is: at home, with a few beers, listening to Coast Guard radio traffic and browsing the stranger corners of the internet.
## What we know
- Rockstar plays him as the paranoid one, the kind of guy who half-believes everything he reads online.
- Monitoring Coast Guard communications would be a handy skill for anyone moving goods by boat, which hints at how he might help the crew.
- His comfortable routine looks likely to be disrupted once Jason and Lucia's plans pick up speed.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll note the missions Cal appears in and anything he unlocks, such as information, jobs or equipment.

articles.title: Boobie Ike
articles.dek: A Vice City street legend who turned his earnings into real estate, a strip club and a recording studio, and now wants a hit record.
facts: Real estate, strip club, recording studio
articles.body:
Boobie Ike is one of Vice City's best-known faces. He made his name on the streets, then turned that money into a business empire that looks legitimate from the outside: property, a strip club and a recording studio.
## What we know
- His biggest passion project is Only Raw Records, the label he runs with Dre'Quan Priest, a hustler with music-mogul ambitions.
- The label has signed rap duo Real Dimez and is chasing its first real hit.
- Rockstar presents him as self-interested but invested in Dre'Quan's success, which could make for an interesting partnership as the label grows.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add his missions, businesses you can visit and any jobs he offers.

articles.title: Dre'Quan Priest
articles.dek: A dealer with music-mogul ambitions, partnered with Boobie Ike at Only Raw Records, who has just signed Real Dimez.
articles.body:
Dre'Quan sold drugs to get by, but music was always the goal. He's spent time booking performers into Boobie Ike's strip club, and now he's partnered with Boobie on Only Raw Records.
## What we know
- He signed rap duo Real Dimez to the label, his first big move.
- With a real act on his books, he's setting his sights on Vice City's wider music scene, which may mean less time working for Boobie's club.
- That ambition could put him at odds with Boobie, though Rockstar hasn't said how the relationship plays out.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the missions he's involved in and any music-business side content.

articles.title: Real Dimez (Bae-Luxe and Roxy)
articles.dek: High school best friends turned social media rap duo, newly signed to Only Raw Records after an early hit with local rapper DWNPLY.
articles.body:
Real Dimez is a duo: Bae-Luxe and Roxy, friends since high school. They built a following on social media and through their rap tracks, and before music took off they made money working with local dealers.
## What we know
- An early single with local rapper DWNPLY gave them their first taste of success.
- They're now signed to Only Raw Records, run by Dre'Quan Priest and Boobie Ike.
- Their story looks set to explore the pressure of going from internet fame to a real career, with plenty of temptation along the way.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add their missions and anything else they unlock.

articles.title: Raul Bautista
articles.dek: A charming, seasoned bank robber who recruits people for risky jobs, which seem to grow more reckless as the game goes on.
facts: Appears to work with Jason and Lucia
articles.body:
Raul is a career bank robber with plenty of experience and plenty of charm. He's always looking for capable people willing to take risks, and the jobs he plans pay well but carry real danger.
## What we know
- Rockstar describes his jobs as increasingly reckless, which suggests anyone working for him will eventually have to decide whether to push their luck or walk away.
- A scene in the second trailer appears to show Jason and Lucia as part of his crew.
- If GTA VI has big, planned heists like earlier games, Raul looks like the most likely person to set them up.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add his heist missions with approach options, crew choices and payouts, written to help you pick the best route.

articles.title: Brian Heder
articles.dek: An old-school smuggler from the Keys' glory days who still moves product through his boatyard, and Jason's landlord.
articles.body:
Brian ran drugs during the golden age of smuggling in the Keys and never really stopped. He still moves product through his boatyard, though these days he prefers to have other people do the dirty work.
## What we know
- Jason lives in one of Brian's properties and does jobs for him in return.
- Cal Hampton is one of his associates.
- His third wife, Lori, works with him at the boatyard.
- He's one of the first faces you see in the second trailer, which suggests he plays an early role in Jason's story.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the jobs Brian gives you, where to find his boatyard, and how his story connects to the main plot.

articles.title: Vice City
articles.dek: Leonida's neon-lit centerpiece, with art deco hotels on Ocean Beach, the busy streets of Little Cuba and a cruise port that calls itself the capital of the world.
facts: Ocean Beach, Little Cuba, VC Port
articles.body:
Vice City returns as the heart of GTA VI. It's a modern take on the series' classic Miami-style city, swapping the 1980s for the present day while keeping the sun, the neon and the excess.
## Places to know
- Ocean Beach, with white sand and pastel art deco hotels
- Little Cuba, a compact, busy neighborhood of narrow streets
- VC Port, which bills itself as the cruise ship capital of the world
## Getting around
Raised freeways and crowded streets make the city slower to cross than the open countryside. Previews suggest that breaking line of sight will matter more than raw speed when you're trying to lose the police here.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll map Vice City's shops, safehouses, side activities and the best escape routes.

articles.title: Leonida Keys
articles.dek: A laid-back island chain of boat parties, dive bars and reef diving. It's also Jason's home turf.
articles.body:
The Leonida Keys are a string of tropical islands south of the mainland, with an easygoing pace to match. It's where Jason lives and works, so expect to spend a good part of the early game here.
## Places to know
- The Rusty Anchor, one of the dive bars Rockstar has highlighted
- Bays full of boat parties
- Brian Heder's boatyard, the base of his smuggling business
## Things to do
Scuba diving is one of the confirmed activities, with turtles and other sea life to find, along with some hazards beneath the surface. With so much water around, boats will be one of the best ways to get around.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add dive spots, boat locations and any Keys side jobs.

articles.title: Grassrivers
articles.dek: Leonida's vast wetlands, full of stilt houses, mangroves, alligators and stranger things hidden in the water.
articles.body:
The Grassrivers are GTA VI's version of the Everglades: miles of marsh and mangrove forest, with buildings on stilts along the edges. It's a world away from Vice City's streets.
## What to expect
- Alligators are the headline attraction, and the area is a hunting spot
- Rockstar warns of deadlier predators below the surface and some disturbing discoveries deeper in
- Other people out here hunting are likely to be armed, so don't assume a quiet swamp is a safe one
## Getting around
Airboats look like the natural choice for crossing the water, and fans have spotted a hovercraft in the trailers.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add hunting spots, hidden locations and any wetland side quests.

articles.title: Port Gellhorn
articles.dek: Leonida's forgotten coast: a faded resort town of empty strip malls and run-down motels, where the drug trade is filling the gap.
facts: Decline, with a new drug economy
articles.body:
Port Gellhorn used to be a tourist destination. Now its glory days are long gone, and what's left is a stretch of tired motels, abandoned attractions and empty strip malls.
## Places to know
- The Starlet Motel
- The Delights cabaret
- Deserted strip malls and closed-down attractions
## What's happening here
Rockstar says the drug trade has moved in to fill the economic gap, creating a new local economy. That points to plenty of criminal opportunity on Leonida's west coast.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add Port Gellhorn's businesses, side jobs and points of interest.

articles.title: Ambrosia
articles.dek: An industrial town by Lake Leonida, built around the Allied Crystal sugar refinery and run by a local biker gang.
articles.body:
Despite the sweet name, there's little sweet about Ambrosia. It's a working industrial town beside Lake Leonida, and most people here depend on the Allied Crystal sugar refinery that dominates the skyline.
## What to expect
- Old-fashioned blue-collar values, enforced by the biker gang that controls the area
- Factories, rail yards and heavy industry rather than beaches
- A very different crowd from Vice City, so expect different kinds of jobs and trouble
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add Ambrosia's missions, the biker gang's role and what's worth visiting.

articles.title: Mount Kalaga National Park
articles.dek: The wild northern border of Leonida, home to hunting, fishing, kayaking, off-road trails and some deeply suspicious locals.
articles.body:
Mount Kalaga National Park forms Leonida's northern edge, a big stretch of forest and hills for anyone who wants to get away from the city.
## Things to do
- Hunting, with deer and mountain lions mentioned by Rockstar
- Fishing and kayaking
- Off-road trails for trucks and bikes
## Who lives here
The backwoods are home to hermits and paranoid types hiding from the government. Some will make for strange encounters, and some may be dangerous.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the best hunting grounds, trail routes and any secrets hidden in the park.

articles.title: GTA 6 Prologue walkthrough: Lucia's first mission
articles.dek: The game opens with Lucia behind bars and a flashback to the job that put her there. It's short, mostly scripted and can't be failed in any meaningful way.
articles.body:
The Prologue starts as soon as you begin a new game. You play as Lucia, who is serving time. Guides name the jail as Hamlet Prison; Rockstar's pre-launch profile called it Leonida Penitentiary, so the in-game name may differ from the marketing.
## Objectives
- Talk to your cellmates. Holding the aim button brings up conversation options, so you can be friendly or pick a fight. It doesn't change the outcome.
- Follow the guard, CO Wilson, down the corridor. He pauses for a phone call, then takes you to a counselor's office. You can chat to other inmates on the way.
- The counselor's questions trigger a flashback: Lucia robbing a payday loan store. Aim at the teller, threaten them and scoop up the cash. A customer tries to tackle you; fight them off.
- Lose the cops. You run across rooftops and through a mechanic's shop, jumping and climbing as prompted.
- Return to the coffee shop marked on your map.
## Tips
- You can't actually escape the chase. Two of the three guides we checked say the game cuts back to the counselor's office whatever you do; one describes losing the police and reaching the coffee shop. Either way the result is the same, so don't waste time trying to outrun the script.
- The arrest at the end can't be avoided. It's a story beat, not a failure.
- This is a good moment to learn the basics: the aim-to-talk system, melee and parkour controls all come back later.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! The coffee shop matters because Lucia left her young son, Tommy, there while she did the robbery. Staff had already called the authorities.
!! Tommy is taken into child welfare and Lucia is arrested. Getting out of prison and back to him becomes her driving goal.
## Next
The story then switches to Jason for Gone Fishing, the second mission. Lucia returns as a playable character later in Chapter 1.

articles.title: GTA 6 Gone Fishing walkthrough: Jason's first job
articles.dek: Jason and Cal pick up a drug drop off the Keys, and a simple job turns into a stealth rescue and a seaplane escape. It also gets you into Jason's house.
articles.body:
Gone Fishing is Jason's introduction. He and Cal are out on Cal's boat waiting for a pilot, Donnie, to drop a shipment into the water.
## Objectives
- Take the wheel when Cal asks and follow Donnie's plane. Steer to each floating package and slow down early so Cal can hook it. There are three. If you lose sight of one, use Focus (both sticks) to find it again.
- Follow the marker to the meeting point and use the zoom to watch Donnie's handover on the dock.
!! The deal goes wrong and Donnie is grabbed by a local gang, the Kingfishers. You need to get him back.
- Bring the boat in quietly and go ashore at the camp, an RV park in the wetlands.
- Sneak through. Crouch, approach guards from behind, grab and subdue them. Tall grass on the edge of the camp gives cover, and you don't need the rifle lying around.
- Find the shack marked on your map, go in and reach Donnie. One guard will rush you; beat him unarmed to keep things quiet, then grab the health item (Zombix) in the shack.
- Optional: a dollar marker leads to a trailer with cash in it. Someone jumps you with a knife on the way in, so be ready for the prompt.
- Get to Donnie's floatplane on the dock and take off over open water. Don't turn back toward the camp if you're taking fire.
- Fly to Brian's Marina. Slow your descent and land on the water short of the dock, then taxi in.
- After the cutscene, drive Cal home, then drive to Jason's house and go up the outside stairs to finish.
## Tips
- Jason starts with almost nothing, so a fight in the open is hard. Knockouts beat gunfire here. There's an optional hammer behind one building if you want a melee weapon.
- The landing is on water, not a runway. Come in slowly and level.
- The trailer cash is worth the detour early in the game, when money is tight.
## Rewards
Finishing the mission opens Jason's house. You can change clothes and get drinks there, and one guide reports you can work on renovating it later, which is said to earn Focus points and improve things with Lucia; that last part isn't confirmed by other guides yet.
## What happens next (spoilers)
!! You meet Brian Heder, the smuggler Donnie flies for and Jason's landlord, at his marina.
!! Lucia gets in touch to say she's being released. Guides differ on whether it's a phone call or a face-to-face talk.
## Next
Gear Up, where Jason buys a long gun, is the next story mission.

articles.title: GTA 6 Gear Up walkthrough: buying Jason's first long gun
articles.dek: A quick trip to Ammu-Nation for a shotgun or rifle, then a scrap with three Kingfishers in the car park. Fight them with your fists and you'll keep the police out of it.
articles.body:
Gear Up follows straight on from Gone Fishing. Now that he's working for Brian, Jason decides he needs something heavier than a pistol and calls an old contact, Andrew, who works the counter at the local Ammu-Nation.
## Before you leave the house
Check the mailbox outside Jason's place. Early on, mission payments are delivered there rather than to a bank account, and one guide has the mission begin with you picking up cash from it. Get in the habit of checking it.
## Objectives
- Take the car parked outside the house and drive to the Ammu-Nation marked on your map.
- Talk to Andrew at the counter and pick a long gun.
- Leave the shop. Three Kingfishers pull up in a truck and come at you.
- Deal with all three, then phone Donnie to warn him the gang is looking for you both. That call ends the mission.
## Which gun to buy
You get a choice between a pump shotgun and a tactical rifle. One guide reports the shotgun at $350 and the rifle at $450, with Jason holding a little over $500, which means you can afford one but not both. Those prices aren't confirmed by other guides yet, and one says most players will only be able to stretch to the shotgun.
- The rifle is the better all-rounder at medium and long range, and if there's money left over a larger magazine is a sensible first add-on.
- The shotgun is cheaper and fine for the close-quarters fights in the next few jobs.
- Either way, the mission plays out the same. Guides agree the choice doesn't change the story.
## Tips
- Use your fists on the Kingfishers. Gunfire in the street draws the police, and you'll have to shake them before you can carry on. A fistfight gets a much slower police response.
- If Jason dies, he wakes up at home and the mission simply ends. You can restart it from the marker.
- Andrew gives Jason a mates' rate because they go back a long way.
## What to do next
Once the call to Donnie is done, the game loosens up. You can explore, start collecting rent for Brian (Lab Fees) and visit Coastal Auto Care (Just a Scratch). Cal also has a job waiting (Unwanted Attention).
## A note on order
Guides don't agree on the order of the early Chapter 1 jobs. Several open up at once after Gear Up and can be done in whichever order you like, so the numbering here follows one guide's chronological list rather than a fixed sequence.

articles.title: GTA 6 Unwanted Attention walkthrough: the impound lot job
articles.dek: Cal takes Jason to Hamlet to lift a red Phoenix out of a police impound. You'll pick up the police scanner, learn how heat works and earn $150.
facts: Cal's marker, north of Jason's house on Key Lento
Red Phoenix in the Hamlet impound
articles.body:
This is the job that teaches you how the police and your 'heat' work. Cal needs a car out of the impound lot in Hamlet to settle something owed to Brian, and Jason is doing the climbing.
## How to start
Look for Cal's 'C' marker a short way north of Jason's house on Key Lento. Guides place him in slightly different spots (on a beach, or fishing off a bridge), so just follow the icon.
## Objectives
- Talk to Cal, get in his truck and drive to Hamlet. On the way Cal sets you up with a police scanner, which from then on lets you listen in on police radio.
- Get into the impound without using the gate. Climbing is the quiet route: guides describe scaling the fence or a gap in the wall and crossing the stacked containers in the back corner. One also mentions a lift at the back that takes you up onto a roof, where you can look over the lot.
- Find the target, a red Phoenix sports car hitched to a tow truck near the back. Your phone can scan cars if you're unsure which one it is.
- Release the Phoenix from the tow truck, get in and hotwire it by moving both sticks into the marked positions.
- Drive to the main gate and wait for it to open. The police will spot you at this point whatever you do; it's scripted. If a guard grabs the car, mash the prompt to shake him off.
- Lose the police. Get out of the flashing search area on the minimap. The wanted level is low, so a few quick turns and a stretch of open road will do it. Keep the car in one piece: wrecking it is the main way to fail.
- Take the Phoenix to the nearby Pay 'n' Spray and respray it. Any colour will do.
- Deliver it to Brian's garage and collect the $150 waiting there.
- Change your look to clear your heat. Buy an outfit at the gun shop next door, or swap hats and glasses from the item wheel. Once the police no longer recognise you, the mission ends.
## Tips
- Don't knock out the impound guards unless you have to. Doing so brings a police patrol to the lot.
- The clothes lesson matters for the rest of the game. Icons on the item wheel show whether the police would still recognise a hat or pair of glasses, and changing outfits or respraying a car makes you harder to spot. One guide suggests keeping a spare outfit in your car's boot.
- Scanning parked cars with the phone also counts towards the vehicle collection, so it's worth doing while you're here.
## A note on order
Guides don't agree on the order of the early Chapter 1 jobs. Several open up at once after Gear Up and can be done in whichever order you like, so the numbering here follows one guide's chronological list rather than a fixed sequence.

articles.title: GTA 6 Lab Fees walkthrough: collecting Brian's rent (door codes)
articles.dek: Brian sends Jason to collect rent from a gift shop in the Keys. The tenant can't pay, so you take something else instead. Door codes: 0420 for the back room, 7700 for Brian's lockup.
facts: A gift shop behind a surf shop, Leonida Keys
articles.body:
Lab Fees is the first of Jason's rent runs for Brian, his landlord. The tenant is a small gift shop tucked in among the bars and surf shops of the Keys.
## How to start
Head for the rent marker on your map. The shop sits behind a surf shop. One guide says the door is locked when you arrive and a call to Brian gets you in.
## Objectives
- Go in and ask the man at the counter for the rent. He says he hasn't got it.
- Lean on him. Either point your gun at him, or wait for him to pull a baseball bat and take it off him. Both get the same result: he offers you what's in the back room instead and gives you the door code.
- Open the keypad door in the corner of the shop with 0420. There's also a note in the shop with the code on it if you miss it.
- Pick up the acid in the back room. There's cash in there too; guides differ on how much is lying around, but grab whatever you find.
- Leave, call Brian and he'll tell you to drop the acid at his lockup further south in the Keys.
- At the lockup, marked with a green icon, enter 7700 and stash the acid. That finishes the job.
## Tips
- You don't have to hurt anyone. If you kill the clerk the code still works, but the police get involved.
- The $600 payment doesn't arrive straight away. Jason has no bank account yet, so it turns up later in the mailbox outside his house.
- Remember the lockup. It's a fence: Brian buys drugs, jewellery and marked cash you come across, so anything like that you find while exploring early on can be turned into money there. More fences open up as the story goes on, each with a green map icon.
- Stolen goods go into a bag, which you can leave in your car's boot.
- Look out for a large whale statue near the shop. It's one of the things you can scan with your phone for the collection.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! The 'gift shop' is a front: the back room is a small acid lab, which is why the tenant pays in product rather than cash.
## A note on order
Guides don't agree on the order of the early Chapter 1 jobs. Several open up at once after Gear Up and can be done in whichever order you like, so the numbering here follows one guide's chronological list rather than a fixed sequence.

sources.name: KeenGamer: chapters and missions in order

articles.title: GTA 6 Just a Scratch walkthrough: free repair at Coastal Auto Care
articles.dek: A short, easy job: take Jason's battered '70 Ganado to Joey at Coastal Auto Care for a free repair and respray. It introduces the game's mod shops.
facts: Coastal Auto Care, near Jason's house
Coastal Auto Care for repairs, mods and tows
articles.body:
Just a Scratch is little more than a tutorial for the game's car shops, but it's mandatory. Jason's car, a '70 Ganado, needs fixing up, and Joey at Coastal Auto Care is the man for it. The waypoint hints it's a favour for Lucia.
## Objectives
- Drive the Ganado from Jason's house to the Coastal Auto Care marker.
- Pull up by the garage door and greet Joey. When the door opens, drive inside.
- In the shop menu, choose the engine repair. It costs nothing during this mission.
- Go to the cosmetics menu and pick a respray. Any colour is fine, and that's free too.
- Drive out. A short scene with Joey plays and the mission is done.
## Tips
- Mods cost money, and you won't have much at this point. Save your cash.
- If you've already wrecked the Ganado, one guide suggests making a manual save and loading it from the pause menu. You'll be back at home with the car outside.
- The free repair is a one-off. After this, repairs at the shop cost money. Coastal Auto Care can also be phoned for a paid tow, which saves a long drive back.
- Don't sink much money into this car. You drive it for the rest of Chapter 1, but it's eventually replaced and one guide reports that any upgrades go with it. Registering a new personal vehicle reportedly opens up in Chapter 2.
- Ultimate Edition owners can pick a free 'Retro Build' body kit in the shop. It's optional.
## Next
Pipework, another of Brian's rent jobs, is next in most guides' order.
## A note on order
Guides don't agree on the order of the early Chapter 1 jobs. Several open up at once after Gear Up and can be done in whichever order you like, so the numbering here follows one guide's chronological list rather than a fixed sequence.

sources.name: Beebom: Just a Scratch mission guide

articles.title: GTA 6 Pipework walkthrough: Mandy's rent and the blocked sink
articles.dek: Brian sends Jason to collect rent from a tenant named Mandy, who won't pay until her kitchen sink is fixed. A plunger, a wrench and a free cigar later, the job's done.
articles.body:
Pipework is Jason's second rent run for Brian. This time the tenant is Mandy, and she has a condition: fix her sink first.
## How to start
Brian phones Jason, usually while you're out driving, and a rent job appears on the map. Guides describe Mandy's place as a blue house on Key Lento in the Keys.
## Objectives
- Drive to Mandy's house and talk to her outside. She says the rent waits until the kitchen sink works.
- Follow her in. She heads to the bedroom rather than the kitchen and keeps talking; you can let her finish or cut in and ask where the plunger is. It makes no difference to the outcome.
- Get the plunger from the bathroom across the hall. It's by the toilet.
- Go to the kitchen and plunge the sink by tapping the prompted button (R3 on PlayStation, per two guides). This alone won't clear it.
- Put the plunger down, get under the sink and use the wrench from the cabinet to open the pipe and pull out whatever's blocking it.
- Mandy makes a pass at Jason during or after the repair. He turns her down. There's no romance option here, however you play it.
- On the way out, pick up the box of cigars from the street outside. That's your Macizo Cigar. Brian then gets in touch to say the rent has arrived, and the mission ends.
## Tips
- You can't really fail this one. Guides agree there's nothing to lose in the sink section.
- Don't drive off without the cigar box. It's the only thing you get out of the job.
- The rent goes to Brian, not Jason, so don't expect money in the mailbox. Guides differ on exactly when Mandy pays: one says she hands it over after the sink is cleared, another that she sends it to Brian during the repair. Either way Brian gets paid.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! Mandy has picked up gossip, reportedly from a bartender at the Rusty Anchor, that Jason has an ex in prison. Only one guide mentions this.
!! Mandy turns up again later in Chapter 1 outside the mission itself, according to one guide.
## Next
Brian calls Jason to a pool bar on Key Lento for Hey Arnold!, the next story job.
## A note on order
Guides number the early Chapter 1 jobs differently because several open up at the same time. We follow the order most guides agree on; if your game offers them in a different order, nothing breaks.

articles.title: GTA 6 Hey Arnold! walkthrough: should you kill or spare Arnold?
articles.dek: Brian, Cal and Jason go looking for a man who has stopped answering Brian's calls. It ends in a car chase, a foot chase and the game's first big choice. Our advice: spare him.
facts: Jason Duval, with Brian and Cal
A pool bar in southern Key Lento
articles.body:
Arnold works for Brian, and he's gone quiet. Hey Arnold! is about finding out why, and it gives you the first real moral choice of the story.
## How to start
After Pipework, Brian calls and asks Jason to meet him at a pool bar in the south of Key Lento. One guide names it as the Crastenburg.
## Objectives
- Meet Brian at the bar and hear him out.
- Follow him to his pickup, take the driver's seat and drive to the liquor store to pick up Cal.
- Head for the search area. A large white blimp in the sky points you toward an old radar station, where Arnold and his crew are.
- After a short scene, Arnold makes a run for it in his car. Chase him in Brian's truck.
- Arnold's men come after you on motorbikes and open fire. Shoot back from the truck.
- Keep going over the broken bridge. The jump is automatic.
- When Arnold's car stops, chase him on foot to the docks.
- At the water's edge, Jason decides what happens to him.
## Kill or spare?
- Kill: the mission ends there. Your criminal profile moves toward the violent end of the scale.
- Spare: Arnold jumps into the sea and swims off. Your profile moves toward 'restrained'.
- Neither choice changes your pay for this job, and guides agree the mission itself plays out the same.
- Guides disagree about later consequences. One says Arnold is gone from the game whichever you choose; two others say sparing him pays off later in the story. If you want to keep your options open, spare him.
## Tips
- Jason's slow-time ability (both sticks at once) makes the shooting on the chase much easier.
- Shooting out one of Arnold's tyres on the bridge can end the car chase early.
- If you shoot Arnold with a loud weapon, leave the docks before the police arrive.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! Arnold has been working against Brian's business, and Jason calls him out on it before the choice.
!! According to two guides, a spared Arnold comes back later in the story for a scene with Brian. This isn't confirmed by every guide.
## Next
Several jobs open up next. Kenton's Island Dreams and Cal's Feng Shui are the next two story missions in most lists.
## A note on order
Guides number the early Chapter 1 jobs differently because several open up at the same time. We follow the order most guides agree on; if your game offers them in a different order, nothing breaks.

articles.title: GTA 6 Island Dreams walkthrough: Kenton's dive, the wreck and the shark
articles.dek: Jason takes a bachelor party scuba diving for Kenton, a dive-shop owner in the Keys, and finds treasure on a shipwreck. It pays $400 and opens up underwater treasure hunting.
facts: Kenton, at the Island Dreams shop
Kenton's boat and shop; wreck diving
articles.body:
Island Dreams is a change of pace: no guns pointed at people, just a dive trip. Kenton runs a dive shop of the same name and needs Jason to babysit some tourists.
## How to start
Look for the 'Work For Kenton' marker at his shop on the east side of Key Lento, near the beach.
## Objectives
- Take Kenton's boat out to the dive spot marked on your map. Keep going until Kenton tells you to stop.
- Put on the scuba gear at the back of the boat and get in the water.
- Lead the three members of the bachelor party along an underwater trench to a shipwreck.
- At the wreck, switch to the metal detector and sweep the marked area. The light goes from red to green, and flashes faster, as you get close. Collect what you find. Guides count two or three pieces of treasure, described as gold coins.
- One of the divers, Dobbs, gets stuck on the wreck. Swim over and lift the grate or hatch that's pinning him.
- On the way back a shark goes for the group. Pick the speargun from your weapon wheel and hit it twice.
- Swim back to the boat for the closing scenes.
## The shark choice
You don't have to shoot. If you leave the shark alone, Dobbs doesn't make it. Two guides say this only changes the dialogue at the end; your $400 and Kenton's offer are the same either way.
## Tips
- Oxygen isn't a worry here. There's plenty of time.
- Aim for the shark's head and allow for the spear's arc, even close up.
- Swimming near fish and other sea life counts toward the animal total for 100% completion.
- After the mission you can come back to Kenton's shop and use his boat. Shipwrecks around the map can be revisited for any treasure you missed.
- Gear like the scuba kit and metal detector is taken off if you spend too long on land.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! The bachelor party is a cover. Kenton is really a treasure hunter and wanted the wreck searched.
!! Jason hands over what he found and agrees to keep working with Kenton, which sets up more dive jobs later.
## Next
Cal's Feng Shui, back at Jason's house, is next in most guides' order.
## A note on order
Guides number the early Chapter 1 jobs differently because several open up at the same time. We follow the order most guides agree on; if your game offers them in a different order, nothing breaks.

articles.title: GTA 6 Feng Shui walkthrough: rearranging Jason's house with Cal
articles.dek: Cal decides Jason's place isn't fit for Lucia's homecoming, so the two of them move the furniture and play video games. No combat, no way to fail.
articles.body:
Feng Shui is one of the quietest missions in the game: an evening in with Cal. It's mandatory, short and a good break after Hey Arnold!
## How to start
Cal texts Jason and a marker appears on his house. Walk in to begin.
## Objectives
- Grab a beer from the fridge and sit on the couch with Cal. He points out that the place needs work before Lucia gets home.
- Move the furniture as prompted: the TV over by the door, the coffee table in front of it, then the couch (talk to Cal until he asks you to move it) and finally the chair from under the lamp.
- Sit down and play the JoyStation console with Cal. The first game is a puzzle game called Tenebrae Lux; after a little while Jason asks to swap.
- The second game is Street Trash III, a top-down shooter. You can't win it. Play until it ends or your character dies, and the closing scene starts.
- The mission wraps up the next morning.
## Tips
- Cal fusses over where the coffee table goes. You can accept it or keep adjusting; guides agree it doesn't matter.
- In Tenebrae Lux, spiked and triple pieces knock out flat ones, according to one guide.
- The JoyStation stays in the house, so you can play it whenever you're back.
## What happens (spoilers)
!! The next morning brings the news Jason has been waiting for: Lucia is being released. Guides differ on whether the call comes from the prison or from Lucia herself.
## Next
Coming Home, where Jason goes to meet Lucia, follows. Before that, a set of optional errands to get the house ready for her opens up.
## A note on order
Guides number the early Chapter 1 jobs differently because several open up at the same time. We follow the order most guides agree on; if your game offers them in a different order, nothing breaks.
